comment: For a first year seminar, I did not learn anything from this class. It was unstructured, confusing, and the directions were very unclear for the assignments resulting in biased grading.

Lots of reading is assigned for each class. Absolutely no need to read all of it. Just read some sections so you can communicate opinions during discussions and in the journals. Only one paper and final project assigned over the entire semester. Final project expectations were somewhat unclear.

Jeannine Keefer's class has absolutely no structure. There is a ton of reading but for no particular goal. Your grade is purely dependent on participation and the final project, so you will not know your grade until the end of the semester. Jeannine's classes are just her rambling the whole time. Not sure why she is a professor, I learned nothing.

Professor Keefer is a very kind person, but a terrible professor. Her classes simply comprised of discussions about very long, pointless readings and you don't learn much at all. She is hard to get in contact with outside of class and is terrible at answering emails. Be prepared to never know your grade throughout the whole semester.

Dr. Keefer is knowledgeable, but the class discussions were sometimes repetitive, often going on tangents. Participate! FYS100 ended with a project with individual & group work. The project requirements were unclear, and she seemed to be figuring out what she wanted the students to submit after the project began. Take her if you like architecture.

One of her strongest points is her availability to meet. This is especially helpful when it comes to her writing assignments: she will be pretty clear about what she wants. There is a lot somewhat boring reading, but that is arguably important for new students. Participate! your grade hinges on it. Grading is tough: anything below a 95 is an A-.

Class participation matters, speak up 3-4 times a lesson and you will be fine. No tests, very relaxing, graded mostly on papers which is also clear and fairly lenient on what she wants. Lead discussions.

solid fys choice pretty easy, each class a group of students leads discussions based on the reading and we just talk the whole time. no final for the class, just a outline of an essay instead. only two short papers and some easy homework. while the topic of architecture is boring, she is great and it is a great fys choice for a A.
no clear grading and no feedback. Classes can be long and repetitive, and participation hinges on reading the books.
The most unclear professor and gets annoyed if you ask to clarify anything. She doesn't grade any assignments until right before grades are due, so you have no idea how you are doing.

why do we build is a solid FYS choice She gives a lot of readings but you don't really have to do them. No tests and the papers/projects are pretty easy. The worst part is you have to go on a few field trips to east end cemetery which is kinda annoying As a person she's nice and goes off on tangents all the time which makes class pretty interesting

Dr. Keefer is really nice and passionate about architecture. It is an easy class. She gives you a bunch of books but you don't have to read them. Just go to class, say something smart and she'll love it. 2 papers, 1 assignment, 1 project, and a reflective journal.

Took her for FYS. It was an extremely easy and interesting class. There are a ton of books and readings but you really dont need to read them all entirely to do well. Theres only 2 papers the whole semester and a group project with reflective journals in between. Overall not a ton of effort required if you participate and are good at writing

Dr. Keefer is knowledgeable on the subject and extremely nice. Attendance is mandatory however if you need days off let her know and she is understanding. Her feedback on papers is minimal so be prepared to find other resources. Most of the class is reading and discussion. I didn't read any of the books completely and still got high essay grades.

Dr. Keefers FYS is super easy. Theres a ton of reading but you don't have to do it, just make something up to say that sounds smart. Semester long group project but not too bad because she helps a lot. Overall, relativly boring but easy FYS
